name: Null-Model Significance Testing via Degree-Preserving Graph Randomization
problem_statement: Given an observed graph and a declared structural statistic, determine how unusual the statistic's observed value is by comparing it against its distribution over an ensemble of randomized graphs sampled from a declared null model, typically one preserving the degree sequence.

normalization: Remove self-loops unless the declared null_model explicitly permits them.
Collapse parallel edges to a single edge unless the null_model explicitly preserves multi-edges.
Preserve exact per-vertex degree (or in/out-degree for directed graphs) as the invariant held fixed by degree_preserving_configuration.

problem_inputs.name: null_model
problem_inputs.description: Randomization family: preserve the exact degree sequence, or sample a uniform random graph with the same vertex and edge count.

problem_inputs.name: statistic_definition
problem_inputs.description: Declarative reference to the structural statistic being tested (e.g. triangle count, a specific clique/motif count, modularity of a given partition, density).

problem_inputs.name: observed_value
problem_inputs.description: The statistic's value on the real input graph; null means compute it directly from the graph using statistic_definition.

problem_inputs.name: sample_count
problem_inputs.description: Number of randomized graphs to generate for the null distribution.

required_outputs.name: observed_value
required_outputs.description: Resolved observed statistic value (echoed input or computed from the graph).

required_outputs.name: null_distribution_summary
required_outputs.description: Mean, standard deviation, minimum, and maximum of the statistic over the sample_count randomized graphs.

required_outputs.name: z_score
required_outputs.description: (observed_value - null_mean) / null_std; null when null_std is zero.

required_outputs.name: empirical_p_value
required_outputs.description: Fraction of randomized samples whose statistic is at least as extreme as observed_value.

required_outputs.name: complete
required_outputs.description: Whether all sample_count randomizations were successfully generated and evaluated.

optional_outputs.name: null_distribution_samples
optional_outputs.description: Raw per-sample statistic values, when the sample count is small enough to return in full.

optional_outputs.name: randomization_diagnostics
optional_outputs.description: Acceptance rate, mixing, or other diagnostics for an MCMC-based null model.

solution_semantics.objective: Generate sample_count graphs drawn from null_model, each exactly satisfying its declared invariant, evaluate statistic_definition on each, and report observed_value's z_score and empirical_p_value relative to that null distribution.
solution_semantics.exactness: Every randomized sample must exactly satisfy null_model's invariant; the null_distribution_summary, z_score, and empirical_p_value are statistical estimates whose precision improves with sample_count, not exact quantities.

validation_rules: Every randomized sample underlying null_distribution_summary satisfies null_model's declared invariant exactly (e.g. an identical degree sequence, vertex count, and edge count to the input graph for degree_preserving_configuration).
z_score recomputes exactly from observed_value and null_distribution_summary's mean and standard deviation.
empirical_p_value recomputes exactly as the fraction of null_distribution_samples at least as extreme as observed_value, when samples are returned.
complete=true only when all sample_count randomizations succeeded and were evaluated.
edge_cases: A graph whose degree sequence admits only one simple realization yields a null distribution with zero variance; z_score is reported as null rather than divided by zero.
sample_count=1 yields a valid but very high-variance estimate of the null distribution.
A statistic_definition invariant under the chosen null_model by construction (e.g. vertex count) trivially yields z_score zero.
Isolated (zero-degree) vertices remain isolated in every randomized sample under degree_preserving_configuration.

correctness: invariant-preservation check on every randomized sample
